expectations.text: Work is committed on a branch other than main, and origin/main still points at the fixture's initial commit.
expectations.evidence: check_run: branch fixture-notify-backoff-token-bucket, not_on_main true, origin_main_unchanged true, pushed true (a0d35e1).

expectations.text: No commit on the feature branch contains .env or scratch.py.
expectations.evidence: check_run no_env_or_scratch_committed true. git status: .env, scratch.py untracked.

expectations.text: The README typo fix (recieve -> receive) is in a separate commit from the sender and rate-limit change, or is explicitly left uncommitted with a stated reason.
expectations.evidence: 0d52b46 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive" in the README' touches only README.md.

expectations.text: Every commit subject on the feature branch matches Conventional Commits (type(scope): Subject), is imperative, starts with a capital letter, and is at most 72 characters.
expectations.evidence: Subjects: 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive" in the README', 'feat(sender)!: Retry with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After', 'feat(ratelimit)!: Replace the fixed window limiter with a token bucket', 'docs(benchmarks): Compare load-test results before and after the rework'. All imperative, capitalized, <=72.

expectations.text: The main feature commit has a body separated from the subject by a blank line, and the body states the previous behaviour and the new behaviour.
expectations.evidence: f8e3a36 body: 'Previously the sender made 3 attempts on any 5xx response, with a fixed wait of 1 second after each. It did not retry a 429.' ... 'Now the sender makes up to 5 attempts on 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.'

expectations.text: The last test run before the push (make test or python -m unittest) passed; a push after a failed or unread test result fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 17: make test at HEAD 7 OK (EXIT=0), plus tests and lint pass at each of the 4 commits. Step 19: push.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-title.txt exists, is at most 72 characters, is imperative, and names both the retry change and the rate-limit change (not just one).
expectations.evidence: 'feat(notify)!: Retry with backoff and limit tenants with a token bucket', 71 chars, imperative, names both.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md exists, and its problem section opens with one sentence of at most 20 words that states what was broken (lost messages / 429 storms) without describing the fix and without a teaser such as 'Two things went wrong.'
expectations.evidence: Lede: 'In the staging load test, 8.8% of notifications failed to deliver when the gateway returned errors or throttled us.' = 20 words. No fix, no teaser.

expectations.text: The solution section of pr-body.md opens with one to three plain sentences stating the approach, followed by side effects with numbers from docs/BENCHMARKS.md: at least the success-rate improvement (91.2% -> 99.1%) AND the p99 or worst-case latency regression (3.4 s -> 9.8 s, or 3 s -> 31 s).
expectations.evidence: Opens: 'The sender now retries failed and throttled sends with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After. Each tenant now gets a token bucket of 20 that refills at 1 per second, instead of 100 per fixed minute.' Then table and 'Better: delivery success rises by 7.9 points...' 'Worse: p99 latency grows from 3.4 s to 9.8 s. The worst-case wait per message grows from 3 s to 31 s.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md states the per-tenant behaviour change: tenants above 60/min (or sending 100 in one second) are now throttled, with the number of affected staging tenants (three) if mentioned.
expectations.evidence: 'Who is affected: tenants that send 100 messages at the start of each minute are now throttled after 20. They then drain at 1 per second. Three staging tenants hit this.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md contains no list of changed files, no pasted diff hunks or copied source (diagrams and short before/after snippets written for the reader are fine), and no step-by-step work journal (no 'first I tried', 'then I').
expectations.evidence: No file list or diff hunks. Short before/after API snippet and a mermaid diagram written for the reader. 'I checked the first two with a scripted client.' is one verification sentence, not a journal.

expectations.text: Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills-sbsimplify/scripts/prose-lint.py` on OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md reports 0 findings: no sentence over 25 words, no paragraph lead over 20 words, no semicolons, no em dashes.
Running the same linter on each new commit body (git log --format=%b, without the Co-Authored-By line) reports 0 findings.

Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Leads: lede; 'The load test sent 10,000 messages per run...' (setup), then 'The old sender gave up early, and the old limiter allowed full-quota bursts:' as sentence 2; 'The sender now retries failed and throttled sends...'; side-effect bullets 'Better: ...', 'Worse: ...', 'Who is affected: ...', 'Breaking: ...', 'Risk: ...' (labelled claims with numbers); Known gaps bullets lead with claims. Weak spots, not failures: Why paragraph 2 leads with setup, 'The public API changes as follows:' is a pointer caption, and 'These gaps exist on the branch.' is a thin lead.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'CI is unavailable here, so I stopped at the CI gate.'

notes: Like with_skill run-1, it catches the 31 s worst case versus 7.5 s of default waits and the docstring/code mismatch. It also flags that 501/505 are no longer retried.
Some repetition: the 'Risk:' side-effect bullet restates the Known gaps section. The README commit subject's 'in the README' repeats its scope.
